assessment.nobel_worthiness: A strongly distinctive visionary voice. The Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid build dense, recursive prose in which body, memory, dream and metaphysical speculation form one imaginative architecture. The linguistic and formal ambition is high, and the work moves across prose and poetry. The imaginative depth looks sustained rather than confined to a single book.
assessment.attribution: A single Romanian-language author. A citation could cover the whole oeuvre, from poetry through the large prose cycles, as a cosmology built from the interior and the corporeal. It need not rest on one title.
assessment.maturity: Decades of work with a coherent, widening project. Recent large-scale books suggest continued development rather than repetition, which supports giving a prize now.
uncertainties: Romanian-language texture, wordplay and the poetic side of the oeuvre may be only partly conveyed in translation, so my assessment of the original prose is limited.
My corpus coverage is uneven: the major novels are better known to me than the early poetry or the shorter prose.
The density and length of the major novels may limit how widely the case can be shared among readers who work in translation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A radically uncompromising dream-logic fiction that destabilizes psychology, space and causality, with few close parallels in contemporary world literature. The formal and imaginative commitment is sustained across a long career. The strangeness is a deliberate method with its own internal rigor, not an ornament.
assessment.attribution: A single Chinese-language author. A citation could name the creation of an autonomous dreamlike narrative world, with Frontier and Love in the New Millennium among the works available in English.
assessment.maturity: A long and consistent body of work, with novels and many stories developing one inventive method. Her late-career productivity continues.
uncertainties: The proportion of the oeuvre available in translation is limited, and I cannot judge how well the translations carry the original Chinese prose.
The works' difficulty makes their reception harder to assess, and I do not know how it would be weighed across the committee.
I have not independently verified the details of the translated corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly original practice that remakes the boundaries among classical scholarship, lyric, essay, translation, narrative and visual form. Autobiography of Red and Nox show formal invention joined to emotional force. The intellectual depth is considerable, and her handling of the book as an object extends the scope of poetry.
assessment.attribution: A single English-language author, with classical translation and scholarship as a significant strand. A citation could address the hybrid form-making across genres, though it would need careful wording to avoid reducing the range to one mode.
assessment.maturity: Decades of consistently inventive work, with influence on contemporary poetry and on hybrid writing. The oeuvre looks mature, though still evolving.
uncertainties: Much of the work's effect depends on its formal and typographic design, which I cannot assess in the abstract.
Scholarly and translated work sits alongside the creative work, and it is unclear how a committee would weigh the two.
How well her work travels in translation into other languages is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mythic, grotesque and satirical forms are used to confront state violence, ideology and the costs of development. The Four Books and The Explosion Chronicles combine moral urgency with deliberate formal experiment. His self-described departure from conventional realism gives the work a recognizable voice.
assessment.attribution: A single Chinese-language author. A citation could cover the sustained invention of a mode of mythic-absurd narration used to critique power and its effects on ordinary lives.
assessment.maturity: A long, productive career with some works constrained by censorship. The tonal range is wide, and the thematic focus is consistent.
uncertainties: Some of the effect rests on political context. I should weigh literary achievement separately from political symbolism, and the line is hard to draw.
Quality across such a large output may be uneven, and my coverage of the untranslated works is limited.
I cannot independently assess how the original prose is rendered in translation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A calm, meditative prose of moral interiority, in which theology, family life and American history meet. Housekeeping and Gilead show a distinctive voice and a rare capacity for sustained attention to inner life. The quiet formal achievement is considerable, and the essays add intellectual depth.
assessment.attribution: A single English-language author. A citation could address the fusion of theological and ethical thought with fiction of great stylistic restraint, covering both the novels and the essays.
assessment.maturity: A relatively small number of novels over several decades, each of high quality, followed by extension into the Gilead sequence. The oeuvre is durable, though compact.
uncertainties: The comparatively small volume of fiction raises the question of breadth.
Her thematic world is closely tied to a particular Protestant and American context, and I am uncertain how readers outside it respond.
The essays and the fiction may be judged differently, and I have not independently verified the details of her reception.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A transformative figure in modern Arabic poetry, working through myth, fragmentation and a sustained argument with inherited poetic forms. Songs of Mihyar the Damascene is central to his formal renewal of the language. The critical essays add to the intellectual scope of the project.
assessment.attribution: A single Arabic-language poet and essayist. A citation could address the renewal of Arabic poetic language and form across a long career, with poetry as the primary achievement.
assessment.maturity: A long, established body of work, with a well-documented place in the Arabic tradition. Timing is not a barrier, given the length of the career.
uncertainties: Translation of poetry that depends so heavily on Arabic prosody and its history inevitably loses much, so my assessment relies on secondary knowledge of the original.
His public and political positions are a separate matter from literary merit and should not distort the assessment either way.
I have not independently verified how complete the available translations are.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large polyphonic novels such as Carpentaria and The Swan Book remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time. The scale, the narrative invention and the sense of a new narrative form drawing on Aboriginal storytelling are distinctive.
assessment.attribution: A single English-language author with a body of fiction and nonfiction. A citation could address the reshaping of the novel through Indigenous narrative traditions, and would need to cover both novels and nonfiction work.
assessment.maturity: A relatively small number of very ambitious books. The oeuvre is still developing, and its long-term durability is harder to judge than for writers with longer careers.
uncertainties: The number of major works is limited, so I cannot be sure about the sustained quality across a full career.
My knowledge of the more recent work is less complete.
The dense, collective voice may be hard to render for readers in other languages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Compressed, densely worked French prose that turns obscure lives and art history into narrative inquiry. Small Lives (Vies minuscules) and The Eleven (Les Onze) show a rare stylistic intensity and a concentrated approach to the relation between art, power and obscurity. The quality is high and the voice is unmistakable.
assessment.attribution: A single French-language author. A citation could address a body of short, intensely wrought books that reinvent the biographical-fictional form.
assessment.maturity: A concentrated and consistent oeuvre rather than a large one, with strong standing in French letters. The lasting quality is probably high.
uncertainties: The compression and syntactic density of the original are very hard to translate, and I cannot assess how well the translations convey it.
The oeuvre is small, so the question of breadth and sustained development is open.
My knowledge of the later works is thinner than for the best-known books.
